pages.title: 1. Copper day
pages.text:
Mine copper and cobblestone. No iron needed yet.

Craft a Copper Gear: four copper ingots around a cobblestone.

Then a Winding Crank and a Mainspring. Right-click the crank with the spring, then hold right-click on the crank with an empty hand. About 20 seconds winds it full.

pages.title: 2. Your first robot
pages.text:
Craft a Clockwork Mechanism and a Wooden Chassis, then Stumpy.

Place Stumpy among trees. Put a chest or Supply Crate right next to it. Right-click Stumpy with the wound Mainspring.

It now fells, replants and fills the chest. Sneak-right-click it to see its status and area.

pages.title: 3. First iron
pages.text:
Make a Tinker's Hammer. Two ingots and the hammer in the crafting grid give one plate.

With your first iron: a Combustion Generator (burns coal or logs), a Charger next to it, and a Copper Cell. Right-click the generator with fuel and the Charger with the cell.

pages.title: 4. Power tools
pages.text:
Craft a Tool Upgrade Kit I. At a smithing table: kit + hammer + Electric Motor make a Bore Drill. Kit + Felling Axe + motor make a Chainsaw.

The drill mines like an iron pickaxe, or 3x3. Press V to switch. Keep a Copper Cell in your inventory: it recharges the drill.

pages.title: 5. Diamonds
pages.text:
Your first diamonds make the Excavator. It digs a big hole straight down to bedrock, slowly.

Feed it speed cards and a lot of power to make it fast. Then go for Advanced Circuits: Age 2 starts.

pages.title: Where to look
pages.text:
This book: click any item to see its recipe, then click the ingredients.

Your recipe book fills up as you go: every step of the guide unlocks the next recipes.

Hold Shift on an item for details and keys. Press L for the Robotica advancements.

pages.title: Five ages
pages.text:
Age 0 Clockwork: copper, wood, stone.
Age 1 Wired: iron, redstone, gold.
Age 2 Servo: diamonds, obsidian, quartz, a Servo Core.
Age 3 Deep: netherite, blaze rods, a Magma Core.
Age 4 Antigrav: ender pearls, nether stars, an Antigrav Core.

The Servo Core drops from the Scrap Colossus (see Bosses). The other cores keep an expensive recipe until their bosses arrive.

pages.title: The parts ladder
pages.text:
Machines are built from parts. Each age's parts eat the parts of the age before: a Reinforced Casing takes four Iron Casings.

Starting is cheap. Getting great costs a lot.

pages.title: Circuits and motors
pages.text: Circuits and motors climb the same ladder. Plates come from the hammer (two ingots each) or the Metal Press (one ingot each). Plates from other mods work too.

pages.title: Making FE
pages.text:
Robotica runs on FE, like Thermal and Mekanism. Their generators power Robotica and the other way round.

Winding Crank: by hand, 2 minutes per Mainspring.
Combustion Generator: any furnace fuel, 80 FE/t.
Solar Panel: 20 FE/t by day, Mk2 80 FE/t.

pages.title: Batteries
pages.text:
Robots carry a battery. A Mainspring runs Stumpy for about 2 hours, a Copper Cell 8, a Redstone Cell 24, an Ender Cell 72.

Right-click a robot with a battery to swap it in. A cell in your inventory recharges the FE tool in your hand.

pages.title: Moving and storing FE
pages.text:
Accumulators store FE and give it out on their front. They keep their charge when broken.

The Charger fills cells and tools. Right-click it with the item.

pages.title: Tesla Coils
pages.text:
Tesla Coils send FE through the air. Put one on an Accumulator or a generator: it sends that block's FE.

Sneak-right-click the coil with a Tesla Linker, then right-click machines. The side you click is where the power goes in. Click it again to unlink.

Link a coil to another coil to reach further. Each hop loses 5%. Every link uses one slot.

Tier I to V: 4, 8, 12, 16 and 32 links, 8 to 32 blocks range, 4,000 to 1,000,000 FE/t. Right-click a coil to see its links.

Hold the Tesla Linker to see every link light up. Without it, finished networks stay quiet.

pages.title: Metal Press
pages.text: One ingot makes one plate: twice what the hammer gives. Right-click it with ingots or feed it with a hopper.

pages.title: New ores
pages.text:
Thorium: Overworld, Y -48 to 32, in stone and deepslate. Common.
Pyrolite: the Nether, most in basalt deltas. Iron pickaxe.
Resonite: end stone on the outer End islands. Rare. Diamond pickaxe.

A Tinker's Hammer cracks raw thorium, shards and crystals into dust. A Grinder doubles ores.

pages.title: Alloy Smelter
pages.text:
Robotica alloys come only from here.

Ferrothorium: iron + thorium (Age 2).
Pyrosteel: ferrothorium + pyrolite + blaze powder (Age 3).
Resonant Alloy: pyrosteel + resonite + ender pearl (Age 4).

The Metal Press or the hammer makes plates of them.

pages.title: Assembler
pages.text:
Up to six inputs, one part. Thermocouples, Superconductor Coils and Resonant Lattices are made nowhere else. Circuits, motors and casings cost about a quarter less here than at the crafting table.

Big parts need a lot of FE.

pages.title: Centrifuge
pages.text: Splits one input into up to four results, some by chance. Depleted Fuel Pellets give thorium dust back and, one time in ten, a Radiant Isotope. It also splits magma cream and glistering melons.

pages.title: Mk1 to Mk4
pages.text:
Every industry machine comes in four Mks. Each Mk works faster (x1, x2, x3, x5) and has one more card slot (2 to 5) with higher caps: speed, efficiency, and from Mk2 fortune (a chance of one more result).

Craft the next Mk from the last one, or right-click a placed machine with the next Mk: it keeps everything inside and you get the old one back.

pages.title: Fuel and the RTG
pages.text:
The Assembler presses thorium dust, graphite and a ferrothorium plate into a Thorium Fuel Pellet.

The Radioisotope Generator burns one at a time: 150 FE/t, silently, for 20 minutes. Build more for more power. Reactors burn the same pellets faster and hotter.

pages.title: Multiblocks
pages.text:
Banks and reactors are hollow boxes. Casing on every edge and corner, casing, glass or ports in the walls, the controller in the middle of a side wall with its screen facing out.

The controller GUI names the first wrong block and where it is. The spyglass button outlines the box and the wrong block in the world.

Ports work with any mod's cables and with Tesla Coils.

pages.title: Capacitor Bank
pages.text:
3x3x3 up to 9x9x9. Fill the inside with Capacitors (storage) and at least one Transfer Coil (speed). Copper 8M, Redstone 64M, Ender 512M FE. Coils add 64k, 512k or 4M FE/t, for input and output each.

Sneak-right-click a Bank Port to switch it between input and output. A broken controller keeps its energy.

pages.title: Fission Reactor
pages.text:
3x3x3 up to 7x7x7. Fuel Rods fill whole columns, floor to roof. Put coolant next to them: water 1, ice 1.5, packed ice 2, blue ice 3, Cryo Coolant 4. Coolant carries the heat away and raises the efficiency.

Fuel pellets go in the controller or an Access Port, waste comes out the same way. Power Ports send the FE out; a Tesla Coil can sit on one.

A 5x5x5 with one rod column makes about 1,000 FE/t, a full 7x7x7 tens of thousands.

pages.title: Heat and SCRAM
pages.text:
More heat than cooling and the reactor heats up. Above 1,000 C the output drops, at 1,800 C it SCRAMs: it shuts itself down. It never explodes and never breaks blocks.

Drag the control rod slider to make less heat. After a SCRAM let it cool, fix the cooling, then press Reset.

Fuel only burns while the power goes somewhere.

pages.title: Fusion Reactor
pages.text:
A 7x3x7 box of Fusion Casing. Inside, one layer: a ring of 16 Fusion Coils around an empty 3x3 chamber. Reactor Glass and Reactor Ports fit in its walls.

Feed 20M FE into a Power Port to charge it, add fusion fuel and it ignites: about 200,000 FE/t. It burns fuel whether you use the power or not. Out of fuel, the plasma collapses and needs a new charge.

pages.title: Stumpy and Sprout
pages.text:
Stumpy fells whole trees, replants and picks up drops. Sprout harvests and replants crops and tills dirt next to water.

Both fill a chest, Supply Crate or storage interface that touches them. A stalled robot smokes and tells you why.

pages.title: Farm tiers
pages.text:
Right-click a placed robot with a Farm Kit to upgrade it.

Mk1: 9x9 (Stumpy one block less on each side). Mk2: 13x13, faster. Mk3: 17x17. Mk4: 25x25, the whole area every pulse.

Each Mk also takes one more speed, range and growth card.

pages.title: Mining Drone
pages.text:
A flying helper for early game. Right-click a block to deploy it, sneak-right-click to pick it up again with everything it carries.

Give it a Copper Cell or Mainspring and some torches. In its menu, turn the drill with the N/E/S/W button, pick a length and press the pickaxe. It digs a 3x3 tunnel, lights it, bridges gaps and brings your loot back.

It turns back for lava, water, a full inventory or low energy. Press H to make the nearest drone dig where you look. Sneak+H calls all drones back.

pages.title: Sentry Drone
pages.text:
Shoots energy bolts at monsters, never at players, pets or villagers.

Guard patrols around a spot, Follow stays with you, Stay holds position. Aggressive attacks every monster in range, Defensive only what attacks you.

Repair it with iron. Speed, range and efficiency cards go in its upgrade slots.

pages.title: Courier Drone
pages.text:
Carries items between inventories. Sneak-click a source and then a target with the drone item or the Courier Remote to link a route (up to 4).

Set a filter in its menu: allow or block list, optional tag matching. It carries one stack per trip, three on Mk2.

Mk2 drones come from the smithing table with an Advanced Circuit and a Servo Actuator, and keep everything inside.

pages.title: Upgrade cards
pages.text:
Right-click a machine or robot with a card, or put it in an upgrade slot.

Speed, Range, Efficiency, Growth and Fortune stack: more cards in the same slot, each card is one step. Silk Touch and Void are single cards.

Speed: x2, x3, x4, x6 ... up to x20 with 8 cards. Each card costs more energy than the one before.

Every machine has its own maximum. Robots take as many speed, range and growth cards as their Mk tier.

pages.title: Digging a real hole
pages.text:
Needs your first diamonds. It mines everything below it, down to bedrock: 8x8, one block every three seconds.

It seals fluids, skips chests and other block entities and never touches bedrock. The GUI shows depth and progress.

pages.title: Making it fast
pages.text:
Up to 8 speed cards (x20), up to 4 range cards (16 to 64 wide), efficiency, fortune or silk, and a void card for junk.

Speed is expensive here: 8 cards cost 21 times the FE per block. Bring a lot of generators.

pages.title: Survey Rig
pages.text:
Age 2: Servo parts, a diamond pickaxe and ender pearls. It mines its chunk without digging a hole.

First it scans its own chunk, from its height down to the bottom, and counts every ore. Then it pulls one ore at a time out of that ledger, as if mined with a pickaxe. Nothing is dug: no hole, no lag.

pages.title: Survey rules
pages.text:
One ore every 5 seconds for 2,000 FE. Up to 8 speed cards (x20), but 8 cards cost 21 times the FE per ore. Fortune or Silk Touch, efficiency and void work too.

The ores it counted turn to stone in the world, so nobody mines them twice. A mined-out chunk is surveyed for good: move on to the next chunk. A Magma Core lets it take ancient debris.

pages.title: Mining tools
pages.text:
Tinker's Hammer (Age 0): 1x1 or 3x3.
Bore Drill (Age 1): iron pickaxe, or 3x3.
Servo Drill (Age 2): adds 5x5 and vein mining.
Magma Drill (Age 3): adds 3x3x3, 9x9, auto-smelt.
Null Drill (Age 4): up to 12x12x12.

FE tools never break. Empty, they mine like wood.

pages.title: Controls
pages.text:
V: next mode. Sneak + V or sneak + scroll: previous.
Hold sneak: always one block.
B: Silk Touch / Fortune / off (Servo and up).
G: settings (keep floor, auto-pickup, void filter, auto-smelt).
Auto-pickup and the void filter are modules: put an Auto-Pickup or Void Filter Upgrade in a power tool at a Tinker's Bench.

The HUD shows the mode. An outline shows what will break.

pages.title: Trees
pages.text: The Felling Axe and Chainsaw cut a whole tree in one swing and plant a sapling from your inventory. The Chainsaw also clears the leaves. Press V for 1x1.

pages.title: Upgrading tools
pages.text:
Every tool upgrades at a smithing table: the age's Upgrade Kit, the old tool, and a part or core. Energy and settings carry over.

Tools take normal enchantments too. Unbreaking lowers the FE per block.

pages.title: Arsenal
pages.text:
Gearblade (Age 0): a fast copper sword.
Shock Baton (Age 1): slows what it hits.
Rivet Gun (Age 2): rapid fire, no ammo.
Arc Blade (Age 3): lightning jumps to three monsters.
Null Lance (Age 4): hold to charge, then a beam through everything in a line.

The batons take Sharpness and Fire Aspect.

pages.title: Scrap Colossus
pages.text:
A rusted copper robot, three blocks tall. It is where Servo Cores come from: it always drops one, plus copper, iron and parts.

Below half health it calls Scrap Drones and overheats now and then: its open core takes double damage.

Only real attacks hurt it. Traps, suffocation, cactus and falls do nothing.

The loot flies to whoever lands the killing blow. Only they can pick it up for two minutes, or until they log out. Everyone close by sees its health bar.

pages.title: Rusted Foundry
pages.text:
Ruined copper halls in plains, deserts and badlands, far apart. The chest inside holds a Signal Flare.

Right-click the Colossus Altar in the middle with a Signal Flare. One Colossus per altar at a time, then the altar cools down for 5 minutes. A cooling altar cannot be mined.

pages.title: The fight
pages.text:
Arms up: a ground slam is coming. Jump as it lands or get 5 blocks away.
Arm swung back: it throws scrap. Keep moving.

Below half health it calls Scrap Drones and overheats now and then: it stands still with its furnace open. Hit it then for double damage.

pages.title: Farming it
pages.text:
Signal Flares are cheap: copper, redstone, gunpowder and an Electric Motor.

Want your own arena? Craft a Colossus Altar from Age 2 parts and wall it in. The Colossus stays near its altar and never breaks blocks.

pages.title: The suit
pages.text:
Four pieces of powered armor. They never break and run on FE.

Charge each piece in the Charger, or carry a cell: it tops the suit up. Wear all four and they share their batteries. An empty suit still protects; only the modules stop.

pages.title: Modules
pages.text:
Press J to see all four pieces, or sneak-right-click a piece in your hand. Drop modules into the slots and click the switch next to one to turn it off.

Every kind works once per suit. A module tells you which piece and which mark it needs; the screen explains when it refuses one.

pages.title: Early modules
pages.text:
Helmet: Night Vision, Auto-Feeder.
Legs: Servo Stride (run faster), Kinetic Generator (walking charges the suit).
Boots: Step Assist (walk up full blocks), Spring Heels, Fall Dampener, Magnet.
Any piece: Capacitor Plating (a bigger battery for that piece).

pages.title: Marks
pages.text:
Smithing upgrades a piece and keeps its energy, modules and core.

Mk2: Reinforced Casing + Servo Actuator. 2 slots.
Mk3: Blazing Casing + Plasma Actuator. 3 slots, netherite-grade.
Mk4: Null Casing + Null Circuit. 4 slots, does not burn.

Every mark has a four times bigger battery.

pages.title: Levels
pages.text:
Many modules come in levels I to III. Craft the next level from the one below plus the next age's circuits. Higher levels do more and often cost less FE, but need a higher mark: level II wants Mk2, level III Mk3 (Age 4 levels Mk4).

The gold pips in the module screen show the level.

pages.title: Servo and Deep modules
pages.text:
Helmet: Solar Weave, Sonar Pulse (N: outlines ores and mobs), Rebreather, Robot HUD.
Chest: Jet Assist (double jump), Med Injector, Hazard Seal (clears poison and wither), Kinetic Shield.
Legs or boots: Dash Thrusters (R).
Boots: Hydro Fins.
Any piece: Power Regulator (less FE for everything).

pages.title: Flight
pages.text: The Flight module needs a Mk3 chestplate and an Antigrav Core to craft. Press K to switch it on and off. It is the hungriest module by far: bring a big battery or a Power Regulator.

pages.title: Core socket
pages.text:
Chestplates from Mk2 on hold one boss core. It is never used up. With all four pieces at Mk2 or better:

Servo Core: O overclocks (Haste II and Speed for 10 s).
Magma Core: fire immunity, burning hits, lava does not slow you.
Antigrav Core: no fall damage, cheaper Flight, faster Dash.

pages.title: Architect Table
pages.text:
An early machine: copper, cobblestone and a Clockwork Mechanism. Feed it cobblestone, wood, glass, ingots or gems; it turns them into matter. Power it with a wound Mainspring in its battery slot or any FE cable.

The table is the middle of the floor of its own plot. Click plots on the grid to plan buildings, then press Build.

pages.title: Buildings
pages.text:
Every plot gets the same 9x9 building: floor, walls with windows, roof with light panels.

Plots next to each other join into one big hall. Each group gets a door facing the table; click the edge of a plot to add or move doors. Click the line between two joined plots to put up an inner wall: first with a doorway, then solid, then open again. Shift-click a built plot to forget it.

pages.title: Styles
pages.text:
Clean Stone works from the start and costs only rustic matter. Smooth Panel, Detailed Stone and Tech Stone need an Iron, Reinforced or Null Casing in the casing slot and cost more.

Every building block also has a normal recipe, so you can repair or extend a building by hand.

pages.title: Capturing essence
pages.text: Right-click a monster with an Essence Vial to take a sample. Eight samples of the same mob fill the vial. Bosses can not be sampled.

pages.title: The replicator
pages.text:
Build a 3x3x3 of Replicator Frame with the Controller in the middle of one side, at least one Replicator Glass and an empty centre. Insert a full vial and power it.

Harvest mode puts loot in the controller as if you killed the mob. Spawn mode makes the real mob. About one cycle a minute.

Blazes, endermen, guardians, ghasts and wither skeletons need a Magma Core in the Core slot, shulkers an Antigrav Core. It is never used up.

pages.title: Warp Pads
pages.text: Age 1, with ender pearls. Name a pad, stand on it and right-click to travel to any pad you own or a friend made public. FE cost grows with distance. A Rift Upgrade lets a pad jump between dimensions.

pages.title: Going home
pages.text:
Sneak-right-click a pad with a Recall Remote to bind it. Hold right-click for three seconds to go home. Getting hit cancels it.

Portal Projectors (Age 4) show a glowing portal. Link two with a Linking Card and step in, in any dimension.

pages.title: Storage Terminal
pages.text:
Age 1. A big sorted chest: 81 slots, a search box (@mod for a mod, #tag for a tag), a sort toggle, a scrollbar and a 3x3 crafting grid. Shift-click an item to move it in or out. Hoppers, drones and pipes reach it from every side.

Not a network: no autocrafting, no unlimited space.

pages.title: Expansions and power
pages.text:
Three expansion slots take one Storage Expansion each: Mk1 +81 slots, Mk2 +162, Mk3 +324, up to 648 in all. Each Mk is built from the one before.

The terminal uses a little FE (2 per tick, +1 per expansion): feed it from any cable or put a cell in the battery slot. Without power nothing new goes in; taking items out, search and crafting always work.
